#### Acura CL | 2000-2003
Looking for Acura CL fuse box diagrams without the guesswork? This article takes a clear, no-nonsense look at the second-generation Acura CL (model code YA4), produced from 2000 to 2003, and includes detailed fuse box diagrams for the 2000, 2001, 2002, and 2003 model years, exact fuse panel locations, and a straightforward explanation of the fuse layout and individual fuse assignments, making electrical troubleshooting feel less like detective work and more like routine maintenance.

FAQ

			
								
							
						
								
							
			Where is the cigar lighter / power outlet fuse in the Acura CL?It is fuse No. 9 in the right passenger compartment fuse block (passenger side).

#### Acura CSX | 2006-2011
The Acura CSX, a subcompact executive sedan, was produced from 2006 to 2011. Known for its sleek design, efficient performance, and premium features, the CSX served as a reliable and stylish option in the luxury compact sedan market, offering a refined driving experience with advanced amenities.

In this article, you will find detailed fuse box diagrams for Acura CSX models produced in 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010 and 2011. These diagrams provide essential information about the vehicle’s electrical systems, including the assignment of each fuse (fuse layout) and relay. This knowledge is vital for addressing electrical maintenance, diagnosing issues, or performing repairs effectively.

This guide serves as a comprehensive reference for understanding the electrical system of the Acura CSX, ensuring that owners and technicians have the information necessary to maintain the performance and reliability of this executive sedan.

#### Acura EL (1.6EL) | 1997-2000
In this article, we focus on the first-generation Acura EL (1.6EL), a compact luxury sedan produced from 1997 to 2000. Known for its reliability, practicality, and efficient performance, the Acura EL served as an entry-level luxury option, combining comfort and advanced features in a compact package.

Here, you will find detailed fuse box diagrams for Acura EL models produced in 1997, 1998, 1999 and 2000. These diagrams provide valuable insights into the vehicle’s electrical systems, helping owners and technicians understand the assignment of each fuse (fuse layout). This information is crucial for effectively diagnosing electrical issues, performing maintenance, or carrying out repairs.

This article serves as a practical guide to the electrical system of the first-generation Acura EL, offering the essential knowledge needed to maintain its functionality and reliability over the years.

In this article, you will find detailed fuse box diagrams for Acura ILX models produced in 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022. These diagrams provide critical insights into the vehicle’s electrical systems, helping owners and technicians understand the assignment of each fuse (fuse layout). This information is invaluable for diagnosing electrical issues, performing maintenance, or addressing repairs efficiently.

This guide is designed to help you better understand the electrical system of the Acura ILX, ensuring that you have the knowledge needed to maintain its functionality and performance throughout its production years.

#### Acura MDX (YD3) | 2014-2020
In this article, we focus on the third-generation Acura MDX (chassis code YD3), a luxury mid-size SUV produced from 2014 to 2020. This generation of the Acura MDX is celebrated for its sophisticated design, advanced technology, and impressive versatility, making it a popular choice for families and enthusiasts of premium SUVs.

Here, you will find detailed fuse box diagrams for Acura MDX models produced in 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2020. These diagrams provide valuable insights into the vehicle’s electrical systems and are indispensable for owners and technicians performing maintenance, diagnosing electrical issues, or making repairs. This generation of the MDX continues to stand out for its reliability and innovative features.

This article serves as a comprehensive guide to understanding the electrical system of the third-generation Acura MDX, ensuring that owners have the knowledge they need to maintain the performance and dependability of this luxury SUV.

The cigar lighter and power outlet fuses in the Acura MDX are located in the Passenger’s Side Interior Fuse Box and are designated as fuses No.14, No.15, and No.27.

Fuse box location

Engine Compartment Fuse Box Type A

Located near the brake fluid reservoir.Push the tabs to open the box.

Engine Compartment Fuse Box Type B

Located near the battery.Push the tabs to open the box.

Engine Compartment Fuse Box Type C (60A, Fan Main)

Located near the «+» terminal on the battery.(Replacement should be done by a dealer).

Driver’s Side Interior Fuse Box Type A

Located under the dashboard.

Driver’s Side Interior Fuse Box Type B (Not available on all model)

Located under the type A driver’s side interior fuse box.Take off the cover to open.

Passenger’s Side Interior Fuse Box

Located on the lower side panel.

Take off the cover to open.

Rear Fuse Box

Located on the left side of the cargo area, under the floor lining.Remove the cover by prying on the edge of the cover using a flat-tip screwdriver.

#### Acura RL (KB1/KB2) | 2005-2012
The second-generation Acura RL (KB1/KB2) is a full-size luxury sedan produced from 2005 to 2012. Renowned for its refined design, advanced technology, and standard Super Handling All-Wheel Drive (SH-AWD), the RL offered a seamless blend of performance and comfort, firmly establishing itself as Acura&#8217;s flagship sedan.

In this article, you will find detailed fuse box diagrams for Acura RL models from 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, and 2012. These diagrams are essential for understanding the vehicle’s electrical systems and troubleshooting potential issues.

The fuse for the cigar lighter and power outlet in the Acura RL is fuse No.9, located in the Driver’s Side Interior fuse box.

Fuse box location

Passenger compartment

The interior fuse boxes are located under the dashboard on the driver’s and passenger’s side.

To remove the lid, put your finger in the notch on the lid, pull it toward you, and take it out of its hinges.

Engine compartment

The primary under-hood fuse box is in the engine compartment on the driver’s side.

The secondary&nbsp;is on the battery.

#### Acura RLX | 2014-2020
The Acura RLX is a full-size luxury sedan that was produced from 2014 to 2020, serving as the flagship model in Acura&#8217;s lineup. Known for its advanced technology, spacious interior, and refined performance, the RLX offered a premium driving experience with features like a powerful 3.5-liter V6 engine and the innovative Sport Hybrid SH-AWD system. This combination of luxury, efficiency, and performance made the RLX a standout choice in the full-size luxury sedan segment.

In this article, you will find detailed fuse box diagrams for Acura RLX models manufactured in 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2020. These diagrams are essential for understanding the car&#8217;s electrical systems and troubleshooting potential issues. You will also find comprehensive information about the locations of the fuse panels within the vehicle.

The fuses for the cigar lighter and power outlets in the Acura RLX are Fuse No.12 and Fuse No.13 located in the passenger’s side interior fuse box.

Fuse box location

Engine Compartment Fuse Box #1

Located near the brake fluid reservoir.

Push the tabs to open the box.

Engine Compartment Fuse Box #2

Located near the battery.

Push the tabs to open the box.

Engine Compartment Fuse Box #3

Located near the «+» terminal on the battery.

Push the tabs to open the box.

Or

Engine Compartment Fuse Box #4

Located inside the left side of the front bumper.Pull the inner fender back, then push the tabs to open the box.

Driver’s Side Interior Fuse Box #1

Located under the dashboard (fuse locations are shown on the label on the under panel).

Driver’s Side Interior Fuse Box #2

Located inside the driver’s side outer panel.

Passenger’s Side Interior Fuse Box

Located on the lower side panel (fuse locations are shown on the cover).

Take off the cover to open.

#### Acura RSX | 2002-2006
The Acura RSX is a sporty compact car that was produced from 2002 to 2006, serving as the successor to the popular Acura Integra. Known for its sleek design, agile handling, and powerful engines, the RSX quickly became a favorite among enthusiasts and drivers looking for a reliable, performance-oriented compact car. Available in both base and Type-S trims, the RSX offered a range of features that combined practicality with driving excitement.

In this article, you will find detailed fuse box diagrams for Acura RSX models manufactured in 2002, 2003, 2004, 2005, and 2006. These diagrams are essential for understanding the car&#8217;s electrical systems and troubleshooting any issues. You will also get comprehensive information about the locations of the fuse panels within the vehicle. Typically, these panels are located in the interior cabin, beneath the dashboard on the driver’s side, and in the engine compartment, providing easy access for maintenance and repairs.

Additionally, the article provides an in-depth explanation of the fuse layout, outlining the specific assignments of each fuse and relay. These assignments include critical systems and components, such as the headlights, power windows, sunroof, air conditioning, audio system, and safety features like airbags and ABS (Anti-lock Braking System). Relays that control key functions, such as the fuel pump, cooling fans, and ignition system, are also detailed.

Whether you&#8217;re addressing an electrical issue, replacing a blown fuse, or performing routine maintenance, this guide equips you with the knowledge needed to ensure your Acura RSX&#8217;s electrical systems function reliably. The RSX remains a beloved model for its performance and versatility, and maintaining its electrical components is vital to preserving its reputation for dependability and driving pleasure. This resource is an invaluable tool for owners and technicians alike, helping to keep the RSX in peak condition.

The fuses for the cigar lighter and power outlets in the Acura RSX are Fuse No.18 (Accessory Power Socket) and Fuse No.3 (Rear Accessory Power Socket, for US models only) located in the passenger compartment.

#### Acura TLX | 2014-2020
In this article, we focus on the first-generation Acura TLX, a luxury sedan produced from 2014 to 2020. Combining advanced technology, a refined design, and engaging driving dynamics, the first-generation TLX was developed as a replacement for both the Acura TL and TSX models, merging their best features into a single, well-rounded offering. This model introduced a new level of sophistication and performance, quickly becoming a popular choice in the luxury sedan market.

Here, you will find detailed fuse box diagrams for Acura TLX models manufactured in 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2020. These diagrams are essential for understanding the car&#8217;s electrical systems, enabling easy identification and replacement of fuses. The article also provides comprehensive information about the locations of the fuse panels, which are typically situated in the interior cabin—usually under the dashboard—and the engine compartment. These panels are easily accessible, making maintenance and troubleshooting more convenient.

Additionally, the guide includes a thorough explanation of the fuse layout, detailing the specific functions of each fuse and relay. These assignments cover a wide range of components and systems, such as headlights, turn signals, power seats, windows, the infotainment system, air conditioning, and safety features like ABS (Anti-lock Braking System) and airbags. Relays controlling systems like the cooling fan, fuel pump, and heated mirrors are also covered.

Whether you are addressing an electrical issue, performing routine maintenance, or simply becoming familiar with your Acura TLX, this resource offers the detailed information you need to keep the vehicle’s electrical systems functioning reliably. As the first iteration of the TLX, this model set a strong foundation for Acura&#8217;s future sedans, offering a blend of comfort, technology, and performance. Understanding its fuse and relay system is a crucial step in maintaining its exceptional performance and reliability.

The fuses for the cigar lighter and power outlets in the Acura TLX are Fuse No.14 (Console Compartment Accessory Power Socket) and Fuse No.40 (Center Pocket Accessory Power Socket) located in the Interior Fuse Box Type A.

In this article, we explore the first-generation Acura TSX (CL9), a premium compact sedan produced from 2004 to 2008. The first-generation TSX is renowned for its precision engineering, sporty handling, and luxurious features, making it a favorite among drivers seeking a blend of performance and refinement. Based on the European Honda Accord, the TSX offered a unique combination of reliability and driver-focused design tailored to the North American market.

This guide provides detailed fuse box diagrams for Acura TSX models manufactured in 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007, and 2008. These diagrams serve as essential references for understanding the car&#8217;s electrical systems. You will also find information about the locations of the fuse panels, which are typically situated in the interior cabin, beneath the dashboard, and in the engine compartment. Additionally, this resource includes a comprehensive breakdown of the fuse layout, explaining the specific assignment of each fuse to various systems and components. These include critical functions such as the vehicle’s headlights, power windows, infotainment system, air conditioning, and safety features like airbags and ABS (Anti-lock Braking System). The guide also covers relays that control components such as the fuel pump, cooling fans, and more.

Whether you&#8217;re diagnosing an electrical issue, replacing a blown fuse, or performing regular maintenance, this article will provide you with the necessary information to maintain your Acura TSX&#8217;s electrical systems effectively. As the model that introduced the TSX nameplate, the first-generation TSX is a significant part of Acura&#8217;s history, known for its excellent driving dynamics and reliability. Understanding its fuse and relay systems is vital to keeping this iconic vehicle running at its best.

The fuse for the cigar lighter/power outlet in the Acura TSX is Fuse No.9 located in the passenger compartment.

Positioned as a sporty and upscale offering, the Vigor featured a unique longitudinally mounted inline-5 engine, advanced engineering, and a focus on comfort and performance. It served as a bridge between Acura&#8217;s compact and full-size luxury models, offering a blend of refinement and spirited driving dynamics.

In this article, you will find comprehensive fuse box diagrams for Acura Vigor models from 1991, 1992, 1993, and 1994. Understanding the layout is essential for diagnosing electrical issues, replacing blown fuses, or upgrading components.

Whether you are an owner maintaining your Acura Vigor or a technician working on its electrical systems, this resource will help you ensure the proper functionality of the vehicle’s electrical architecture. With its blend of innovative features and timeless design, the Acura Vigor remains a noteworthy model in Acura’s history, and understanding its fuse and relay system is key to preserving its performance and reliability.

#### Audi A3 (8V) | 2012-2020
The third-generation (Mk3) Audi A3 and S3 (chassis code 8V), Audi’s compact luxury car and its high-performance variant, was produced from 2012 to 2020. Combining sleek design, cutting-edge technology, and exceptional performance, this generation of the A3 and S3 stands as a benchmark in the premium compact car segment.

In this article, you will find detailed fuse box diagrams for Audi A3 and S3 models produced in 2012, 2013, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2020. These diagrams offer valuable information on the fuse layout and relay assignments, making it easy to maintain and troubleshoot the vehicle’s electrical systems.

What’s Included:

Fuse Box Diagrams: Easy-to-read diagrams for accurate identification of fuses.

Fuse Panel Locations: Clear instructions on locating the fuse panels within the car.

Fuse Assignments: Detailed descriptions of each fuse and relay, allowing for precise troubleshooting and maintenance.

This guide is a must-have resource for Audi A3 and S3 (8V) owners and technicians, providing the knowledge needed to address electrical issues, replace fuses, or perform routine maintenance. Whether you&#8217;re a DIY enthusiast or a professional, this comprehensive guide simplifies the process of keeping your vehicle in peak condition.

Stay in control of your Audi A3/S3 (8V) with this thorough fuse box diagram guide!

The cigar lighter / power outlet fuse in the Audi A3/S3 is fuse №F40 located in the Instrument Panel.

Passenger compartment

Main Fuse

#### Audi A4 (B9-8W) | 2015-2019
The fifth-generation (Mk5) Audi A4 and S4 (chassis codes B9/8W), Audi’s premium luxury sedan and its high-performance variant, has been produced from 2015 to 2024. Known for its innovative technology, refined design, and impressive performance, this generation of the A4 and S4 has solidified its reputation as a leader in the luxury sedan market.

In this article, you will find detailed fuse box diagrams for Audi A4 and S4 models produced in 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018 and 2019. These diagrams provide valuable insights into the vehicle’s electrical systems, helping owners and technicians understand the assignment of each fuse (fuse layout). This information is crucial for diagnosing electrical issues, performing maintenance, or addressing necessary repairs.

This guide is an indispensable resource for understanding the electrical system of the fifth-generation Audi A4 and S4, ensuring that owners have the tools and knowledge to maintain the functionality, reliability, and performance of these luxurious sedans.

The cigar lighter / power outlet fuse in the Audi A4/S4 is fuse No.6 located in the Black Fuse Panel C within the Driver’s/Front Passenger’s Footwell Fuse Box.

#### Audi A4 (B9-8W) | 2020-2025
The facelifted fifth-generation (Mk5) Audi A4 and S4 (chassis codes B9/8W), Audi&#8217;s luxury sedan and its high-performance variant, has been produced in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. Renowned for its sleek design updates, cutting-edge technology, and refined performance, the facelifted A4 and S4 continue to dominate the premium sedan segment.

In this article, you will find detailed fuse box diagrams for Audi A4 and S4 models produced from 2020 to 2024. #### Audi A6 (C6-4F) | 2004-2011
The third-generation (Mk3) Audi A6 and S6 (chassis codes C6/4F), Audi’s premium mid-size luxury sedan and its high-performance variant, was produced from 2004 to 2011. Known for its elegant design, advanced engineering, and powerful performance options, this generation of the A6 and S6 solidified its position as a leader in the luxury sedan market.

In this article, you will find detailed fuse box diagrams for Audi A6 and S6 models produced between 2004 and 2011. These diagrams provide critical insights into the vehicle’s electrical systems, helping owners and technicians understand the assignment of each fuse (fuse layout). This information is essential for diagnosing electrical issues, performing maintenance, or completing necessary repairs.

This guide is a comprehensive resource for understanding the electrical system of the third-generation Audi A6 and S6, ensuring that owners have the tools and knowledge needed to maintain the functionality, reliability, and performance of these sophisticated sedans.

The cigar lighter (power outlet) fuses in the Audi A6 are as follows:

Fuse A12 (Rear Lighter) in the Trunk Fuse Box.

Fuse A2 (Front Lighter) in the Right Instrument Panel Fuse Box.

Fuse A4 (Center Console Outlet) in the Right Instrument Panel Fuse Box.

Fuse A5 (Trunk Power Outlet) in the Trunk Fuse Box.

The fifth-generation Audi A6 and S6 (chassis codes C8/4K), Audi’s premium mid-size luxury sedan and its high-performance variant, has been available from 2018 to the present. Known for its cutting-edge technology, refined design, and dynamic performance, the A6 and S6 continue to set benchmarks in the luxury sedan market.

In this article, you will find detailed fuse box diagrams for Audi A6 and S6 models produced in 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. These diagrams provide crucial insights into the vehicle’s electrical systems, helping owners and technicians understand the assignment of each fuse (fuse layout). This information is essential for diagnosing electrical issues, performing maintenance, or addressing necessary repairs.

This guide serves as an indispensable resource for understanding the electrical system of the fifth-generation Audi A6 and S6, ensuring that owners have the knowledge and tools needed to maintain the reliability, functionality, and performance of these luxurious and innovative sedans.

What’s Included
Toggle
Fuse Box LocationFuse Box DiagramsLeft footwell fuse panelRight footwell fuse panelLeft cockpit fuse panelRight cockpit fuse panel
Fuse Box Location

The fuses are located in the left and right footwells, as well as at the left and right front sides of the cockpit.

Switch the ignition and all electrical equipment off.

Check the table that follows to see which fuse belongs to the affected equipment.

Use a screwdriver to remove the appropriate cover.

Remove the colored plastic bracket from the fuse panel, if present.

Remove the fuse.

Replace the blown fuse only with a fuse that has the same amp rating.

Reinstall the plastic bracket, if present.

Install the cover.

Fuse Box Locations

Dashboard

Open the driver’s door.

#### Audi Q7 (4M) | 2015-2020
In this article, we focus on the second-generation Audi Q7 (chassis code 4M), a luxurious mid-size SUV available from 2015 to the present. Known for its sophisticated design, cutting-edge technology, and versatile performance, the second-generation Q7 has been a benchmark in the luxury SUV segment.

Here, you will find detailed fuse box diagrams for Audi Q7 models produced in 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2020. These diagrams provide crucial insights into the vehicle’s electrical systems, helping owners and technicians understand the assignment of each fuse (fuse layout). This knowledge is essential for troubleshooting electrical issues, performing maintenance, or carrying out repairs.

This guide serves as a practical resource for understanding the electrical system of the second-generation Audi Q7, ensuring that owners have the information necessary to maintain the reliability, functionality, and performance of this premium SUV.

Fuse Box Location

Open the glove compartment, remove the damper (arrow 1) from the lower holder by applying forward pressure, disengage the glove compartment by pressing on both tabs (arrows 2) and fold it down.

After replacing a fuse, press the glove compartment upward until it engages and reattach the damper.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for BMW 3-Series models produced between 1998 and 2005, covering years 1998, 1999, 2000, 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, and 2005. Engine Compartment

Fuse Box Location

It is situated in the engine compartment on the passenger side, close to the window.

Note: On right-hand drive vehicles, the fuses are located on the opposite side of the engine compartment.

Use the vehicle&#8217;s onboard tool kit to loosen the three cover screws. Next, squeeze the retaining holder and lift it upward. Remove the cover from one side, then press the four retaining clips to fully remove the cover and access the fuse box.

#### BMW 5 (E60) | 2003-2010
The fifth-generation BMW 5-Series (chassis codes E60 for the sedan and E61 for the touring) was produced from 2003 to 2010. Known for its bold design, advanced technology, and impressive performance, this generation marked a significant evolution in BMW&#8217;s luxury mid-size segment.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for BMW 5-Series models produced between 2003 and 2010, covering years 2003, 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, and 2010. These diagrams provide essential details about the fuse layout and relay assignments, helping owners and technicians efficiently maintain and troubleshoot the vehicle&#8217;s electrical systems.

What’s Included:

Fuse Box Diagrams: Clear, detailed visuals to easily identify fuses and relays.

Fuse Panel Locations: Step-by-step instructions on where to locate the fuse panels inside the car.

Fuse Assignments: Comprehensive descriptions of the function of each fuse and relay to simplify diagnostics and repairs.

Whether you&#8217;re addressing an electrical issue, replacing a blown fuse, or conducting routine maintenance, this guide is a must-have resource for BMW 5-Series (E60/E61) owners and technicians. It provides the knowledge and tools needed to keep the car&#8217;s systems functioning optimally.

Maintain the reliability and performance of your BMW 5-Series (E60/E61) with this detailed fuse box guide!

Fuses on the battery

Fuse Box Location

Located in the luggage compartment, under the lining.

The distribution box on the battery is secured on the vehicle battery by means of a metal tab. The metal tabs must be pressed downward and outward in order to release the distribution box.

The distribution box on the battery is equipped with fuses for the following electric loads:Front fuse carrier (250 A)Rear fuse carrier (100 A)Engine compartment distribution box (100 A)– large electric fan (850 W or 1000 W)Electric coolant pump (100 A)Intelligent battery sensor IBS

Fuse Box Location

The fuse box is situated beneath the glove compartment.

Fuse Box Access Instructions

To access the fuse box:

Remove the screws using the screwdriver from the onboard vehicle tool kit.

Remove the cover, carefully unwinding the footwell lamp cable if necessary.

Release the retaining fastener.

Fold the current distributor downward and pull it forward to access the fuse box.

Reinstall all components by following these steps in reverse order.

Engine Compartment

Fuse Box Location

The underhood fuse block is in the engine compartment, on the driver side of the vehicle. To remove the fuse block cover, press the clips on the cover and lift it straight up.

Do not pull the engine compartment fuse block lever, since it is intended only for service purposes. If pulled, vehicle malfunction may occur.

Fuse Box Location

Additional fuses are located in the relay center, on the passenger’s side, below the instrument panel. Engine Compartment

Fuse Box Location

The fuse block is located under the hood in the engine compartment on the driver’s side of the vehicle. Remove the primary cover by pressing the two locking tabs. Remove the secondary cover by snapping off while lifting. To reinstall the fuse panel cover, reverse the sequence.

Passenger Compartment

Fuse Box Location

The instrument panel fuse block is located behind the glove box.

To access the fuse panel:

Open the glove box.

Starting at the bottom, carefully remove the access panel.

Once the retaining clips release, lift the panel away by disengaging the lower tabs from the instrument panel.

To reinstall the panel, insert the bottom tabs into their slots first, then rotate the panel into place until the retaining clips securely engage.

Passenger Compartment

Fuse Box Location

The instrument panel fuse block is located behind the driver-side instrument panel storage compartment.

To access the fuses, press and release the center of the compartment door near the top to open it. Then squeeze the retaining tabs on both sides of the compartment until they clear the instrument panel. Allow the compartment to swing downward to expose the fuse box.

There are relays on the rear side of the fuse block. To reach them, press the tabs and take out the fuse block.

Passenger Compartment

Fuse Box Location

The instrument panel fuse block is located to the right of the glove box.

How to access the fuses:

To access the fuse panel, remove the trim panel starting from the top. After the retaining clips release, lift the panel away, allowing the lower tabs to disengage from the instrument panel.

To reinstall the panel, insert the lower tabs into their slots first, then rotate the panel back into position until the clips securely engage.

#### Cadillac Seville | 1992-1997
Browse Cadillac Seville fuse box diagrams for 1992–1997 models with relay locations, fuse assignments, panel diagrams, and electrical layout information. This article covers the fourth-generation Cadillac Seville, produced from 1992 to 1997, and includes fuse box diagrams for Cadillac Seville 1992, 1993, 1994, 1995, 1996 and 1997, along with details about the location of the fuse panels inside the vehicle and a clear explanation of the assignment of each fuse and relay (fuse layout).

Fuse Box Location

Passenger Compartment

Fuse Box Location

The fuse box is located behind the cover on the driver’s side of the instrument panel.

To access, remove the panel, starting at the top. Once clips are disengaged, the tabs along the bottom of the door can be disengaged from the instrument panel to remove the door.

To reinstall the door, place the bottom tabs into the slots, and rotate the door into position, engaging the clips.

FAQ

			
								
							
						
								
							
			Where are the cigar lighter / power outlet fuses in the Chevrolet Avalanche?2001–2002: In the engine compartment fuse box (fuses “AUX PWR” and “CIGAR”).2003–2006:Engine compartment fuse box: “AUX PWR” (console outlet) and “CIG LTR” (cigarette lighter).Passenger compartment fuse box: “AUX PWR 2, M/GATE” (rear cargo area / midgate outlet).

#### Chevrolet Avalanche | 2007-2013
Explore Chevrolet Avalanche fuse box diagrams in this practical guide that explains the electrical layout of the second-generation full-size pickup. In this article, we consider the second-generation Chevrolet Avalanche (Model Code: GMT900), produced from 2007 to 2013, and provide fuse box diagrams for Chevrolet (Chevy) Avalanche 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012 and 2013, along with information about the location of the fuse panels and the assignment of each fuse and relay (fuse layout).

Fuse Box Locations

Passenger Compartment

It is located on the side of the instrument panel, on the driver’s side, behind the cover.

Center Instrument Panel

The center instrument panel utility block is located underneath the instrument panel, to the left of the steering column.

Passenger Compartment

Fuse Box Location

The instrument panel fuse block is located to the right of the glove box.

To access the fuses:

Remove the outer trim cover. Using a flat-bladed plastic tool, release the retaining clips.

Pull the cover rearward to clear the tab and remove it.

Remove the front panel, starting at the top.

Once the panel clips disengage, allow the tabs along the bottom to release from the instrument panel and remove the door.

To reinstall:Start with the front panel. Insert the bottom tabs into the slots and rotate the door into position until the clips engage. Repeat the same process to reinstall the outer trim cover.

FAQ

			
								
							
						
								
							
			Where are the cigar lighter / power outlet fuses in the Chevrolet Captiva?They are located in the instrument panel fuse box. Check the fuses labeled “CIGAR” (cigarette lighter), “APO JACK (CONSOLE)”, and “APO JACK (REAR CARGO)” (auxiliary power outlets).

Passenger Compartment

The fuse box is located on the driver’s side of the instrument panel, behind the cover.

Engine Compartment

It is located in the engine compartment (left-side).

FAQ

			
								
							
						
								
							
			Where are the cigar lighter / power outlet fuses in the Chevrolet Cavalier?They are located in the instrument panel fuse box. Check the fuses labeled “CIG” (cigarette lighter) and “APO” (accessory power outlet, if equipped).

FAQ

			
								
							
						
								
							
			Where is the cigar lighter / power outlet fuse in the Chevrolet Cobalt?It is located in the engine compartment fuse box. Look for the fuse labeled “OUTLET” or “LTR.”

#### Chevrolet Colorado | 2015-2022
Explore Chevrolet Colorado fuse box diagrams in this clear guide that outlines the electrical layout of the second-generation midsize pickup. In this article, we consider the second-generation Chevrolet Colorado, produced from 2011 to 2022, and provide fuse box diagrams for Chevrolet (Chevy) Colorado 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022, along with information about the location of the fuse panels and the assignment of each fuse and relay (fuse layout).

Fuse Box Locations

Passenger Compartment

The instrument panel fuse box is located under the glove box, behind the passenger side cowl side trim panel.

Engine Compartment

The fuse box is located in the engine compartment (on the driver’s side).

Under-hood Lamps Fuse

The fuse is under the hood on the driver’s side-marker lamp assembly. If you need to keep the hood open for an extended period of time, remove the fuse.

Ride Control Fuse

Vehicles equipped with the optional Real-Time Damping ride control system are protected with a fuse located in the ABS compartment behind the driver’s seat. To access this fuse, pull back the carpet, remove the screw and lift the cover.

Fuse Box Locations

Passenger Compartment

The passenger compartment fuse box is located under the glovebox, in the front-passenger footwell (remove the carpet and toe-board covering).

Engine Compartment

The fuse box is located in the engine compartment (on the right side).

Fuse Box Location

The instrument panel fuse block is behind the glove box. The glove box can be accessed by unlatching the door damper and squeezing the pivot to release the damper ring. Pull the glove box bin side walls in to release the door stops. Then turn the door until the hinge hooks release from hinge pin.

Passenger Compartment

Fuse Box Location

The instrument panel fuse block is located to the right of the glove box.

To access the fuses:

Remove the outer trim cover using a flat-bladed plastic tool to release the retaining clips.

Pull the cover rearward to clear the tab and remove it.

Remove the front panel, starting at the top.

Once the clips disengage, release the tabs along the bottom and remove the panel.

To reinstall:Insert the bottom tabs of the front panel into the slots, rotate it into position, and engage the clips. Then reinstall the outer trim cover in the same way.

FAQ

			
								
							
						
								
							
			Where is the cigar lighter / power outlet fuse in the Chevrolet Monte Carlo?The cigar lighter / power outlet fuse is fuse №1 (Instrument Panel and Console Cigar Lighter) located in the instrument panel fuse box.

#### Chevrolet Monte Carlo | 2000-2005
Explore Chevrolet Monte Carlo fuse box diagrams in this detailed guide covering the electrical layout of the sixth-generation model. In this article, we consider the sixth-generation Chevrolet Monte Carlo (Model Code: GMX230), produced from 2000 to 2005, and provide fuse box diagrams for Chevrolet (Chevy) Monte Carlo models from 2000, 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004 and 2005, along with information about the location of the fuse panels and the assignment of each fuse and relay (fuse layout).

Fuse Box Locations

Passenger Compartment (Driver’s Side)

It is located on the driver’s side of the instrument panel, behind the cover.

Passenger Compartment (Passenger’s Side)

It is located on the passenger’s side of the instrument panel, behind the cover.

Engine Compartment

There are two fuse blocks that are located in the engine compartment, on the passenger’s side.

Fuse Box Locations

Dashboard (Left side)

It is located on the driver side edge of the instrument panel.

Dashboard (Right side)

It is located on the passenger side edge of the instrument panel.

To access the back of the fuse block:1. Push the tab at the top of block down;2. Pull the top of the block outward;3. Reverse Steps 1-2 to reinstall.

Front Compartment

Fuse Box Location

The underhood compartment fuse block is in the front compartment, on the passenger side of the vehicle. Press the clips on the sides and lift the cover to access the fuse block.

Dashboard (Driver&#8217;s Side)

Fuse Box Location

The instrument panel fuse block is on the driver side of the instrument panel, between the steering wheel and the door.

Remove the screw at the bottom of the panel.

Carefully pull the panel from the bottom to release the clips.

Detach the tabs at the top of the panel.

To reassemble, reverse Steps 1-3.

Dashboard (Passenger&#8217;s Side)

Fuse Box Location

The instrument panel fuse block is located behind the glove box. It is accessible by removing the hush panel located underneath the glove box. To remove the hush panel, remove the four push-pins that secure the hush panel.

Relays Center

Relay Box Location

There is a relay center located in the area where the convertible top is stored when it is open.

Open the convertible top until the roof tonneau and the boot cover panel are upright so that you can reach into the convertible top storage area as shown.

Locate the water-tight box that houses the relay center and remove the four nuts that secure the cover to the backside of the passenger compartment.

Press in the tabs on the sides of the cover and lift to remove the cover.

Locate the relay center inside the box. It is located toward the driver’s side of the vehicle. Press in the tabs at each end of the relay center cover and lift to remove.

Reverse the steps to reinstall the relay center cover and close the water-tight box.

FAQ

			
								
							
						
								
							
			Where are the cigar lighter (power outlet) fuses in the Chevrolet Suburban?2000–2002: In the engine compartment fuse box — fuses “AUX PWR” and “CIGAR”.2003–2006:  Engine compartment fuse box: “AUX HVAC” (console power outlet) and “CIG LTR” (cigarette lighter).  Instrument panel fuse box: “AUX PWR 2” / “AUX PWR 2, M/GATE” (rear cargo/luggage compartment power outlet).

Fuse Box Locations

Passenger Compartment

The right instrument panel fuse block access door is on the passenger side edge of the instrument panel. Pull off the cover to access the fuse block. A fuse puller is available on the right instrument panel end cap.

Engine Compartment

Lift the cover to access the fuse block.

Luggage Compartment

The rear compartment fuse block is behind the access panel on the left side of the compartment. Pull the panel out by grabbing the finger access slot at the rear edge.

There are relays on the back of the fuse block. To access, press the tabs and remove the fuse block.

Fuse box locations

Engine compartment

The Power Distribution Center is located in the engine compartment near the battery. This center contains cartridge fuses, mini-fuses, micro-fuses, circuit breakers, and relays. A label that identifies each component is printed on the inside of the cover.

Passenger compartment

The interior fuse panel is located in the passenger compartment on the left side dash panel behind the cover.

To configure the outlets, be sure the ignition is OFF before removing the fuse. The “reconfigurable” fuse location is a special design that allows the fuse to be installed in two different ways. If the fuse is located in the “Upper or Top Position” the outlets will work at all times. If the fuse is located in the “Lower or Bottom Position” the power outlets will only work when the ignition is ON.

#### Chrysler Crossfire | 2004-2008
This guide covers the Chrysler Crossfire (2003–2007), a two-seat sports car. Here you’ll find fuse box diagrams for Chrysler Crossfire 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007 and 2008, along with information about the locations of the fuse panels inside the vehicle and the functions of each fuse (fuse layout).

What’s Included
Toggle
Fuse box locationsEngine compartmentMain fuse boxRelay Control ModulePassenger compartmentFuse box diagramsEngine CompartmentMain fuse boxRelay Control ModulePassenger compartmentFAQ
Fuse box locations

Engine compartment

Main fuse box

The engine compartment fuses are located under the hood on the driver’s side, between the brake master cylinder and the left front fender.

To remove the lid, squeeze the tabs together located at the front of the fuse box. Then lift the lid up by the tabs. The lid will then slide off the top of the fuse box. To replace the lid, place the two hinge-like tabs at the rear of the lid under the tabs on the fuse box. Push down on the front of the lid until the tabs at the front click.

Relay Control Module

The relay control module fuses are located in the Control Module Box next to the battery in the engine compartment.

Passenger compartment

The access door is located on the end of the instrument panel on the driver’s side behind the trim panel cover.

Use a coin or flat blade screwdriver to open and close this access door.

Fuse box location

Gasoline

The Power Distribution Center (PDC) is located in the engine compartment near the battery. Remove the cover by unlatching the two locks located at each side of the PDC cover, avoid the usage of screw drivers or any other tool to remove the cover, since they may apply excessive force and result in a broken/ damaged part. After service is done, secure the cover with its two locks.

A label that identifies each component is printed on the inside of the cover.

Fuse box locations

Configurations:

The type of electrical system in your vehicle is determined by its equipment level. To determine which electrical system your vehicle has, lift the bonnet: if you see an extra fusebox located in front of the battery, it signifies that you have a type 2 system. Conversely, a type 1 electrical system lacks any fuses positioned in front of the battery.

Dashboard

Left-hand drive vehicles: the fuse box is located in the lower dashboard (left-hand side).

Unclip the cover by pulling at the top right, then left, disengage the cover completely, by carefully pulling in the direction indicated by the arrow.

Right-hand drive vehicles:

Open the glove box, unclip the cover by pulling at the top left, then right, disengage the cover completely, by carefully pulling in the direction indicated by the arrow.

Engine compartment

It is placed in the engine compartment near the battery (left-hand side).

An additional fuse box is fitted in front of the battery, for type 2.

FAQ

			
								
							
						
								
							
			Which fuses control the cigar lighter/power outlets in the Dodge Charger?The cigar lighter/power outlets in the Dodge Charger are protected by fuses №12, №38, and №61 (if equipped) in the Rear Power Distribution Center located in the trunk.

#### Dodge Charger | 2024-2026
Explore Dodge Charger fuse box diagrams in this clear guide designed to help you understand the electrical layout of the newest generation. Here we cover the eighth-generation Dodge Charger (2024–present), also marketed as the Dodge Charger Daytona (Model Code: LB), and provide fuse diagrams for 2024, 2025 and 2026, along with the location of the fuse panels and the assignment of each fuse, giving you a straightforward reference for electrical troubleshooting.

Engine compartment

Fuse box location

The Front Power Distribution Center is located in the engine compartment on the left side, positioned in the corner near the windshield when viewing the vehicle from the front. The easiest access point is from the front right wheel area.

Locations

Passenger compartment

It is located in the left kick panel behind the cover.

Engine Compartment

The Power Distribution Center (PDC) is located on the left side of the engine compartment.A description of each fuse and component may be stamped on the inside cover, otherwise, the cavity number of each fuse is stamped on the inside cover.

An integrated power module (IPM) is located on the left side of the engine compartment.A description of each fuse and component may be stamped on the inside cover, otherwise the cavity number of each fuse is stamped on the inside cover.

FAQ

			
								
							
						
								
							
			Where are the cigar lighter/power outlet fuses located in the Dodge Durango?2011–2013 models: The power outlets and cigar lighter are protected by fuses M7 (Power Outlet #2 – Switchable) and M36 (Power Outlet) in the engine compartment fuse box.2014 and newer: The fuses are F90/F91 (Selectable Power Outlet – rear seats), F93 (Cigar Lighter) and F104 (Power Outlets – instrument panel/center console), also located in the engine compartment fuse box.

Fuse box location

The Power Distribution Center is located in the engine compartment near the battery jump start posts.

This center contains cartridge fuses, micro fuses, relays, and circuit breakers. A description of each fuse and component may be stamped on the inside cover, otherwise the cavity number of each fuse is stamped on the inside cover

Fuse box locations

Passenger compartment

The fuse panel is located on the right side below the glove box (remove the bottom of the glove box).

Engine compartment

The power distribution box is located in the engine compartment.

Luggage Compartment

The fuse panel is located in the luggage compartment behind the left side wheel well

Pre-Fuse Boxes

Your vehicle has a pre-fuse box attached to the power distribution box.There is a second pre-fuse box attached to the 12-volt battery terminal in the rear of your vehicle. They contain high-current fuses. If you need to replace one of these fuses, see an authorized dealer.

#### Ford Contour | 1995-2000
The Ford Contour, a mid-size sedan, was produced from 1995 to 2000 as part of Ford’s global platform strategy, sharing many components with its European counterpart, the Ford Mondeo. Known for its responsive handling, fuel efficiency, and comfortable ride, the Contour was a popular choice for daily commuters and families.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for Ford Contour models produced between 1995 and 2000, covering years 1995, 1996, 1997, 1998, 1999, and 2000. 2002–2003 (Instrument Panel Fuse Box):

Fuse №39: E Traveler Power Point #1

Fuse №26: Cigar Lighter

Fuse №40: Power Point #2 (2nd Row Seating Position – Driver Side / Body B-Pillar)

Fuse box locations

Passenger compartment

The fuse panel is located below and to the left of the steering wheel by the brake pedal.

Engine compartment

The power distribution box is located in the engine compartment.

Relay modules:

Instrument panel relay module

The instrument panel relay module is located behind the radio in the center of the instrument panel

Engine compartment relay module

The engine compartment relay module is located in one of two places depending on which type of engine your vehicle is equipped with:Gasoline engine: driver side of the engine compartment above the brake master cylinder.Diesel engine: passenger side of the engine compartment behind the power distribution box.

#### Ford E-Series (E-150, E-250, E-350, E-450) | 2009-2012
The fourth-generation Ford E-Series (E-150, E-250, E-350, E-450), after its third refresh, was produced from 2009 to 2012. Renowned for its reliability, versatility, and strong towing capacity, this model remained a top choice for commercial fleets, cargo transport, ambulances, and passenger shuttles.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for Ford E-Series models produced between 2009 and 2012, covering years 2009, 2010, 2011, and 2012. These diagrams provide essential insights into the fuse layout, helping fleet operators, mechanics, and technicians locate and understand the function of each fuse and relay.

What’s Included:

Fuse Box Diagrams – Clear and detailed visuals to help identify fuses, relays, and circuit breakers.

Fuse Panel Locations – Step-by-step guidance on where to find the fuse panels inside the Ford E-Series.

Fuse Assignments – Comprehensive descriptions of each fuse and relay function for accurate diagnostics and troubleshooting.

Whether you&#8217;re searching for the fuse panel layout, replacing a blown fuse, or diagnosing an electrical issue, this guide is an essential resource. It ensures that your Ford E-Series’ electrical system remains functional and reliable for commercial use, heavy-duty hauling, and long-distance travel.

Keep your Ford E-Series (2009–2012) performing at its best with this detailed fuse box, fuse panel, and relay guide!

The cigar lighter/power outlet fuses (sll are located in the Engine Compartment Fuse Box) in the Ford E-Series are:

Fuse №65: Power Point 2 (Glove Box)

Fuse №66: Power Point 3 (Left-Hand B-Pillar)

Fuse №67: Power Point 1 (Instrument Panel)

Fuse №72: Cigar Lighter

Fuse box locations

Passenger compartment

The fuse panel is located to the left of the brake pedal and mounted onto the lower left cowl panel.

Engine compartment

The power distribution box is located in the engine compartment.

#### Ford E-Series (E-150, E-250, E-350, E-450) | 2015-2020
The fourth-generation Ford E-Series (E-150, E-250, E-350, E-450), after its third refresh, was produced from 2015 to 2020. This iteration of the E-Series continued to be a workhorse for commercial fleets, cargo transport, and passenger shuttles, thanks to its durable construction, powerful engine options, and extensive customization possibilities.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for Ford E-Series models produced between 2015 and 2020, covering years 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2020. These diagrams provide essential insights into the fuse layout, helping fleet operators, mechanics, and technicians locate and understand the function of each fuse and relay.

What’s Included:

Fuse Box Diagrams – Clear and detailed visuals to help identify fuses, relays, and circuit breakers.

Fuse Panel Locations – Step-by-step guidance on where to find the fuse panels inside the Ford E-Series.

Fuse Assignments – Comprehensive descriptions of each fuse and relay function for accurate diagnostics and troubleshooting.

Whether you&#8217;re searching for the fuse panel layout, replacing a blown fuse, or diagnosing an electrical issue, this guide is an essential resource. It ensures that your Ford E-Series’ electrical system remains functional and reliable for commercial use, cargo hauling, and passenger transport.

Keep your Ford E-Series (2015–2020) operating efficiently with this detailed fuse box, fuse panel, and relay guide!

The cigar lighter/power outlet fuses (all are located in the Engine Compartment Fuse Box) in the Ford E-Series are:

Fuse №65: Power Point 2 (Glove Box)

Fuse №66: Power Point 3 (Cutaway B+)

Fuse №67: Power Point 1 (Instrument Panel)

Fuse №72: Cigar Lighter / Power Point

Fuse box locations

Passenger compartment

The fuse panel is located to the left of the brake pedal and mounted onto the lower left cowl panel.

Engine compartment

The power distribution box is located in the engine compartment.

Fuse Box Locations

Passenger compartment

The fuse panel is located behind a trim panel on the left side of the driver’s footwell near the parking brake behind the cover.

To remove the trim panel, slide the release lever to the right then pull the trim panel out.To remove the fuse panel cover, press in the tabs on both sides of the cover, then pull the cover off.

To reinstall the fuse panel cover, place the top part of the cover on the fuse panel, then push the bottom part of the cover until it clicks into place. Gently pull on the cover to make sure it is secure.

To reinstall the trim panel, align the tabs on the bottom of the panel with the grooves, push the panel shut and slide the release lever to the left to secure the panel.

Engine compartment

The power distribution box is located in the engine compartment.

#### Ford Edge | 2015-2024
The second-generation Ford Edge, available from 2015 to 2024, features a sleek design, advanced technology, and a range of powerful engine options. As a midsize crossover SUV, it is well-suited for families, commuters, and adventure seekers, offering a balance of performance, comfort, and utility.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for Ford Edge models produced between 2015 and 2024, covering years 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024. These diagrams provide essential insights into the fuse layout, helping vehicle owners, mechanics, and technicians locate and understand the function of each fuse and relay.

What’s Included:

Fuse Box Diagrams – Clear and detailed visuals to help identify fuses, relays, and circuit breakers.

Fuse Panel Locations – Step-by-step guidance on where to find the fuse panels inside the Ford Edge.

Fuse Assignments – Comprehensive descriptions of each fuse and relay function for accurate diagnostics and troubleshooting.

Whether you&#8217;re searching for the fuse panel layout, replacing a blown fuse, or diagnosing an electrical issue, this guide is an essential resource. It ensures that your Ford Edge’s electrical system remains functional and reliable for daily commutes, long road trips, and weekend adventures.

Keep your Ford Edge (2015–2024) running at its best with this detailed fuse box, fuse panel, and relay guide!

The cigar lighter/power outlet (All are located in the Engine Compartment Fuse Box.) fuses in the Ford Edge are:

Fuse №5: Power Point 3 – Back of Console

Fuse №10: Power Point 1 – Driver Front

Fuse №16: Power Point 2 – Console Bin

Fuse №17: Power Point 4 – Luggage Compartment

Fuse box locations

Passenger compartment

The fuse panel is located under the instrument panel to the left of the steering column.It may be easier to access the fuse panel if you remove the finish trim piece.

Engine compartment

The power distribution box is located in the engine compartment (left-side).

Power Distribution Box – Bottom

There are fuses located on the bottom of the fusebox.

To access the bottom of the fuse box, do the following:

1. Release the two latches, located on both sides of the fusebox.2. Raise the inboard side of the fusebox from the cradle.3. Move the fuse box toward the center of the engine compartment.4. Pivot the outboard side of the fusebox to access the bottom side.

#### Ford Escape | 2020-2022
The fourth-generation Ford Escape, before its facelift, was available from 2020 to 2022. This model introduced a sleek new design, enhanced fuel efficiency, and advanced technology, making it a popular choice for families, commuters, and adventure-seekers.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for Ford Escape models produced between 2020 and 2022, covering years 2020, 2021, and 2022. These diagrams provide crucial insights into the fuse layout, helping vehicle owners, mechanics, and technicians locate and understand the function of each fuse and relay.

What’s Included:

Fuse Box Diagrams – Clear and detailed visuals to help identify fuses, relays, and circuit breakers.

Fuse Panel Locations – Step-by-step guidance on where to find the fuse panels inside the Ford Escape.

Fuse Assignments – Comprehensive descriptions of each fuse and relay function for accurate diagnostics and troubleshooting.

Whether you&#8217;re searching for the fuse panel layout, replacing a blown fuse, or diagnosing an electrical issue, this guide is an essential resource. It ensures that your Ford Escape’s electrical system remains functional and reliable for daily driving, road trips, and outdoor adventures.

Keep your Ford Escape (2020–2022) in peak condition with this detailed fuse box, fuse panel, and relay guide!

The cigar lighter/power outlet (All are located in the Engine Compartment Fuse Box.) fuses in the Ford Escape are:

Fuse №61: Rear Cargo Power Point

Fuse №70: Rear Console Power Point

Fuse №71: Media Bin Power Point

Fuse box locations

Passenger Compartment

The fuse box is located in the passenger compartment below the glove box (remove the bottom).

Engine Compartment

Accessing the Under Hood Fuse Box

Pull the latch toward you and remove the top cover.

Pull the connector lever upward.

Pull the connector upward to remove it.

Pull both latches toward you and remove the fuse box.

Turn the fuse box over and open the lid.

Engine Compartment

Fuse Box Location

Fuse box is located on the driver side in the under hood compartment.

Pull the latch toward you and remove the top cover.

Pull the connector lever upward.

Pull the connector upward to remove it.

Pull both latches toward you and remove the fuse box.

Turn the fuse box over and open the lid.

#### Ford Escape Hybrid | 2010-2012
The second-generation Ford Escape Hybrid, produced from 2010 to 2012, was one of the early hybrid SUVs offering fuel efficiency, eco-friendly performance, and reliable technology. This model combined gasoline and electric power to provide an efficient yet practical driving experience, making it a top choice for urban drivers, families, and environmentally conscious consumers.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for Ford Escape Hybrid models produced between 2010 and 2012, covering years 2010, 2011, and 2012. These diagrams provide essential insights into the fuse layout, helping vehicle owners, mechanics, and technicians locate and understand the function of each fuse and relay.

What’s Included:

Fuse Box Diagrams – Clear and detailed visuals to help identify fuses, relays, and circuit breakers.

Fuse Panel Locations – Step-by-step guidance on where to find the fuse panels inside the Ford Escape Hybrid.

Fuse Assignments – Comprehensive descriptions of each fuse and relay function for accurate diagnostics and troubleshooting.

Whether you&#8217;re searching for the fuse panel layout, replacing a blown fuse, or diagnosing an electrical issue, this guide is an essential resource. It ensures that your Ford Escape Hybrid’s electrical system remains functional and reliable for fuel-efficient driving, long road trips, and daily commutes.

Keep your Ford Escape Hybrid (2010–2012) running efficiently with this detailed fuse box, fuse panel, and relay guide!

The cigar lighter (power outlet) fuses in the Ford Escape Hybrid are:

Fuse №40: Front Power Point (located in the Instrument Panel Fuse Box)

Fuse №3: Rear Power Point (located in the Engine Compartment Fuse Box)

Fuse box locations

Passenger compartment

The fuse panel is located on the right-hand side of the center console, by the instrument panel.

Remove the panel cover to access the fuse cover. Press the tabs on the top and bottom of the fuse cover to remove.

Engine compartment

The power distribution box is located in the engine compartment (left-side).

Auxiliary relay box

The relay box is located in the engine compartment on the radiator support bracket.

Fuse box locations

Passenger compartment

This fuse box is located behind the cover on the instrument panel.

Engine compartment (Power Distribution Box)

Lift the release lever at the rear of the cover to remove it.

Power Distribution Box – Bottom

There are fuses on the bottom of the fuse box. To access the bottom of the fuse box:

1) Release the two latches on both sides of the fuse box.2) Raise the rear side of the fuse box from the cradle.3) Move the fuse box toward the rear side of the engine compartment and rotate as shown.4) Pivot the rear side of the fuse box to access the bottom side.5) Release the two latches to open the fuse cover.

High Current Fuse Box

It is located in the engine compartment below the engine compartment fuse box. This box contains several high current fuses.

Pre-Fuse Box

It is attached to the positive battery terminal.

#### Ford Excursion | 2000-2006
The Ford Excursion (Model Code: UW137), produced from 2000 to 2006, was one of the largest SUVs ever built, offering exceptional towing capacity, a spacious interior, and rugged durability. Designed for heavy-duty use, the Excursion was a favorite among large families, off-road adventurers, and those needing serious hauling power.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for Ford Excursion models produced between 2000 and 2006, covering years 2000, 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, 2005, and 2006. These diagrams provide essential insights into the fuse layout, helping vehicle owners, fleet operators, and technicians locate and understand the function of each fuse and relay.

Fuse Assignments – Comprehensive descriptions of each fuse and relay function for accurate diagnostics and troubleshooting.

Whether you&#8217;re searching for the fuse panel layout, replacing a blown fuse, or diagnosing an electrical issue, this guide is an essential resource. It ensures that your Ford Expedition’s electrical system remains functional and reliable for road trips, off-road driving, and heavy-duty towing.

Keep your Ford Expedition (1997–2002) in top condition with this detailed fuse box, fuse panel, and relay guide!

The cigar lighter / power outlet fuses in the Ford Expedition vary by model year:

1997–1998:

Fuse №3: Cigar Lighter (located in the Instrument Panel Fuse Box)

Fuse №10: Auxiliary Instrument Panel Power Point (located in the Engine Compartment Fuse Box)

Fuse №11: Auxiliary Console Power Point (located in the Engine Compartment Fuse Box)

Since 1999:

Fuse №3: Cigar Lighter (located in the Instrument Panel Fuse Box)

Fuse №1: Power Point (located in the Engine Compartment Fuse Box)

Fuse №4: Console Power Point (located in the Engine Compartment Fuse Box)

Fuse box locations

Passenger compartment

The fuse panel is located below and to the left of the steering wheel by the brake pedal.

Engine compartment

The power distribution box is located in the engine compartment.

1997-1998

1999-2002

The primary battery fuses (megafuses) are located in the engine compartment near the battery.

The engine mini fuses are located on the drivers side of the engine compartment.

#### Ford Expedition | 2003-2006
The second-generation Ford Expedition (Model Code: U222), produced from 2003 to 2006, introduced a fully independent rear suspension, enhanced towing capacity, and improved interior comfort. As a full-size SUV, it remained a popular choice for families, off-road adventurers, and towing enthusiasts.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for Ford Expedition models produced between 2003 and 2006, covering years 2003, 2004, 2005, and 2006. These diagrams provide essential insights into the fuse layout, helping vehicle owners, mechanics, and technicians locate and understand the function of each fuse and relay.

What’s Included:

Fuse Box Diagrams – Clear and detailed visuals to help identify fuses, relays, and circuit breakers.

Fuse Panel Locations – Step-by-step guidance on where to find the fuse panels inside the Ford Expedition.

Fuse Assignments – Comprehensive descriptions of each fuse and relay function for accurate diagnostics and troubleshooting.

Whether you&#8217;re searching for the fuse panel layout, replacing a blown fuse, or diagnosing an electrical issue, this guide is an essential resource. It ensures that your Ford Expedition’s electrical system remains functional and reliable for long road trips, off-road performance, and heavy-duty towing.

Keep your Ford Expedition (2003–2006) running at its best with this detailed fuse box, fuse panel, and relay guide!

The cigar lighter (power outlet, all are located in the Passenger Compartment Fuse Box) fuses in the Ford Expedition are:

Fuse №37: Cargo Area Power Point

Fuse №39: Instrument Panel or Floor Console Power Point, Rear Console Power Point

Fuse №41: Cigar Lighter

Fuse box location

Passenger compartment fuse panel

The fuse panel is located under the right-hand side of the instrument panel behind the cover

To remove the trim panel for access to the fusebox, pull the panel toward you and swing it out away from the side and remove it.To reinstall it, line up the tabs with the grooves on the panel, then push it shut.

To remove the fuse box cover, place a finger behind the PULL tab and your thumb above the PULL tab as shown in the illustration, then pull the cover off.To reinstall the fusebox cover, place the top part of the cover on the fuse panel, then push the bottom part of the cover until you hear it click shut. Gently pull on the cover to make sure it is seated properly.

#### Ford Expedition | 2007-2014
The third-generation Ford Expedition (Model Code: U324), before its 2015 facelift, was produced from 2007 to 2014. This model introduced a stronger frame, improved suspension, and enhanced towing capacity, making it a versatile full-size SUV ideal for families, road trips, and heavy-duty hauling.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for Ford Expedition models produced between 2007 and 2014, covering years 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, and 2014. These diagrams provide essential insights into the fuse layout, helping vehicle owners, mechanics, and technicians locate and understand the function of each fuse and relay.

What’s Included:

Fuse Box Diagrams – Clear and detailed visuals to help identify fuses, relays, and circuit breakers.

Fuse Panel Locations – Step-by-step guidance on where to find the fuse panels inside the Ford Expedition.

Fuse Assignments – Comprehensive descriptions of each fuse and relay function for accurate diagnostics and troubleshooting.

Whether you&#8217;re searching for the fuse panel layout, replacing a blown fuse, or diagnosing an electrical issue, this guide is an essential resource. It ensures that your Ford Expedition’s electrical system remains functional and reliable for off-road adventures, towing heavy loads, and daily commutes.

Keep your Ford Expedition (2007–2014) running at its best with this detailed fuse box, fuse panel, and relay guide!

The cigar lighter (power outlet) fuses in the Ford Expedition vary by model year:

2007–2008 (Engine Compartment Fuse Box):

Fuse №10: Rear Console Power Point

Fuse №41: IP/Console Power Point

Fuse №51: Cargo Power Point

Fuse №52: Cigarette Lighter

Since 2009 (Engine Compartment Fuse Box):

Fuse №65: Auxiliary Power Point (Instrument Panel)

Fuse №66: Auxiliary Power Point (Rear of Center Console)

Fuse №71: Auxiliary Power Point / Cigar Lighter

Fuse №72: Auxiliary Power Point (Right Rear Quarter Panel)

Fuse box locations

Passenger compartment

The fuse panel is located under the right-hand side of the instrument panel behind the cover.

To remove the trim panel for access to the fuse box, pull the panel toward you and swing it out away from the side and remove it.To reinstall it, line up the tabs with the grooves on the panel, then push it shut.

To remove the fuse box cover, press in the tabs on both sides of the cover, then pull the cover off.To reinstall the fuse box cover, place the top part of the cover on the fuse panel, then push the bottom part of the cover until you hear it click shut. Gently pull on the cover to make sure it is seated properly.

Engine compartment

The power distribution box is located in the engine compartment.

#### Ford Expedition | 2015-2017
The third-generation Ford Expedition (Model Code: U324), after receiving its 2015 facelift, was produced from 2015 to 2017. This update introduced a powerful EcoBoost engine, improved suspension, and upgraded technology, making it one of the most capable full-size SUVs for families, towing, and off-road adventures.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for Ford Expedition models produced between 2015 and 2017, covering years 2015, 2016, and 2017. These diagrams provide essential insights into the fuse layout, helping vehicle owners, mechanics, and technicians locate and understand the function of each fuse and relay.

What’s Included:

Fuse Box Diagrams – Clear and detailed visuals to help identify fuses, relays, and circuit breakers.

Fuse Panel Locations – Step-by-step guidance on where to find the fuse panels inside the Ford Expedition.

Fuse Assignments – Comprehensive descriptions of each fuse and relay function for accurate diagnostics and troubleshooting.

Whether you&#8217;re searching for the fuse panel layout, replacing a blown fuse, or diagnosing an electrical issue, this guide is an essential resource. It ensures that your Ford Expedition’s electrical system remains functional and reliable for road trips, off-road adventures, and towing heavy loads.

Keep your Ford Expedition (2015–2017) in peak condition with this detailed fuse box, fuse panel, and relay guide!

The cigar lighter (power outlet) fuses (All are located in the Instrument Panel Fuse Box) in the Ford Expedition are:

Fuse №33: 110-Volt AC Power Point

Fuse №66: Auxiliary Power Point (Rear of Center Console)

Fuse №71: Auxiliary Power Point / Cigar Lighter

Fuse №72: Auxiliary Power Point (Right Rear Quarter Panel)

Fuse box locations

Passenger compartment Fuse Box

The fuse panel is located under the right-hand side of the instrument panel behind the cover.

To remove the trim panel for access to the fuse box, pull the panel toward you and swing it out away from the side and remove it.To reinstall it, line up the tabs with the grooves on the panel, then push it shut.

To remove the fuse box cover, press in the tabs on both sides of the cover, then pull the cover off.To reinstall the fuse box cover, place the top part of the cover on the fuse panel, then push the bottom part of the cover until you hear it click shut. Gently pull on the cover to make sure it is seated properly.

Engine compartment Fuse Box

The power distribution box is located in the engine compartment.

#### Ford Explorer | 2002-2005
The third-generation Ford Explorer (U152), known for its enhanced safety, improved suspension, and more powerful engine options, was produced from 2002 to 2005. This model continued to be a popular choice among families, off-road enthusiasts, and towing professionals, thanks to its spacious interior and rugged capability.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for Ford Explorer models produced between 2002 and 2005, covering years 2002, 2003, 2004, and 2005. These diagrams provide essential insights into the fuse layout, helping vehicle owners, mechanics, and technicians locate and understand the function of each fuse and relay.

What’s Included:

Fuse Box Diagrams – Clear and detailed visuals to help identify fuses, relays, and circuit breakers.

Fuse Panel Locations – Step-by-step guidance on where to find the fuse panels inside the Ford Explorer.

Fuse Assignments – Comprehensive descriptions of each fuse and relay function for accurate diagnostics and troubleshooting.

Whether you&#8217;re searching for the fuse panel layout, replacing a blown fuse, or diagnosing an electrical issue, this guide is an essential resource. It ensures that your Ford Explorer’s electrical system remains functional and reliable for daily driving, off-road trips, and towing needs.

Keep your Ford Explorer (2002–2005) in peak condition with this detailed fuse box, fuse panel, and relay guide!

The cigar lighter (power outlet) fuses are as follows:

Fuse №24: Cigar Lighter (located in the Instrument Panel Fuse Box)

Fuse №7: Power Point #2 (located in the Engine Compartment Fuse Box)

Fuse №9: Power Point #1 (located in the Engine Compartment Fuse Box)

Fuse box location

Passenger compartment

The fuse panel is located below the instrument panel on the driver’s side.

Passenger compartment fuse panel (top side)

These relays are located on the reverse side of the passenger compartment fuse panel.

Pull the panel cover outward to access the fuses.

Engine compartment

The power distribution box is located in the engine compartment.

Auxiliary relay box

The relay box is located on the front right fender well.

Rear Relay Box

The relay box is located on the rear passenger side quarter trim panel.

#### Ford Explorer | 2006-2010
The fourth-generation Ford Explorer (U251), known for its rugged design, enhanced safety features, and improved towing capacity, was produced from 2006 to 2010. This model continued the Explorer&#8217;s legacy as a versatile and capable midsize SUV, suitable for both on-road and off-road adventures.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for Ford Explorer models produced between 2006 and 2010, covering years 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, and 2010. These diagrams provide essential insights into the fuse layout, helping vehicle owners, technicians, and mechanics locate and understand the function of each fuse and relay.

What’s Included:

Fuse Box Diagrams – Clear and detailed visuals to help identify fuses, relays, and circuit breakers.

Fuse Panel Locations – Step-by-step guidance on where to find the fuse panels inside the Ford Explorer.

Fuse Assignments – Comprehensive descriptions of each fuse and relay function for accurate diagnostics and troubleshooting.

Whether you&#8217;re looking for the fuse panel layout, replacing a blown fuse, or diagnosing an electrical issue, this guide is an invaluable resource. It ensures that your Ford Explorer’s electrical system remains functional and reliable for daily driving, towing, and outdoor adventures.

Keep your Ford Explorer (2006–2010) running smoothly with this detailed fuse box, fuse panel, and relay guide!

The cigar lighter (power outlet) fuses in the Ford Explorer are:

Fuse №21: Rear Power Point

Fuse №25: Front Power Point/Cigar Lighter

Both are located in the Engine Compartment Fuse Box.

#### Ford Explorer | 2011-2015
The fifth-generation Ford Explorer (U502), before receiving its 2016 facelift, was produced from 2011 to 2015. This generation marked a significant shift from a traditional body-on-frame SUV to a unibody crossover design, offering improved fuel efficiency, modern technology, and a more comfortable ride.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for Ford Explorer models produced between 2011 and 2015, covering years 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, and 2015. These diagrams provide essential insights into the fuse layout, helping vehicle owners, technicians, and mechanics locate and understand the function of each fuse and relay.

What’s Included:

Fuse Box Diagrams – Clear and detailed visuals to help identify fuses, relays, and circuit breakers.

Fuse Panel Locations – Step-by-step guidance on where to find the fuse panels inside the Ford Explorer.

Fuse Assignments – Comprehensive descriptions of each fuse and relay function for accurate diagnostics and troubleshooting.

Whether you&#8217;re looking for the fuse panel layout, replacing a blown fuse, or diagnosing an electrical issue, this guide is an invaluable resource. It ensures that your Ford Explorer’s electrical system remains functional and reliable for daily commutes, road trips, and off-road adventures.

Keep your Ford Explorer (2011–2015) in peak condition with this detailed fuse box, fuse panel, and relay guide!

The cigar lighter (power outlet) fuses in the Ford Explorer are as follows:

Fuse №32: 110V AC Power Point in the Instrument Panel Fuse Box

In the Engine Compartment Fuse Box:

Fuse №9: Power Point #2 (Console Rear)

Fuse №17: 110V AC Power Point

Fuse №20: Power Point #1 / Cigar Lighter

Fuse №21: Power Point #3 (Cargo Area)

Fuse №27: Power Point (Console)

Fuse Box Locations

Engine Compartment

The under-hood fuse box is located on the driver’s side, near the windshield wiper.

Remove the top cover to reach the fuse box, then remove the fuse box cover to access the fuses.

Passenger Compartment

The passenger compartment fuse box is located under the glove box.

To access it, open the glove compartment, then push the tabs inward to release the detent and fully lower the glove compartment.

#### Ford F-150 | 1997-2004
The tenth-generation Ford F-150, a full-size pickup truck celebrated for its performance, durability, and versatility, was produced from 1997 to 2004. With its modernized design and improved features, this generation solidified the F-150’s reputation as a top choice for work and recreation.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for Ford F-150 models produced between 1997 and 2004, covering years 1997, 1998, 1999, 2000, 2001, 2002, 2003, and 2004. These diagrams provide essential details about the fuse layout and relay assignments, helping owners and technicians troubleshoot and maintain the vehicle’s electrical systems effectively.

What’s Included:

Fuse Box Diagrams: Clear and detailed visuals for quick identification of fuses and relays.

Fuse Panel Locations: Step-by-step guidance on where to find the fuse panels inside your Ford F-150.

Fuse Assignments: Comprehensive explanations of each fuse and relay’s function for diagnostics and repairs.

Whether you are replacing a blown fuse, addressing an electrical issue, or performing routine maintenance, this guide is an invaluable resource for Ford F-150 owners and technicians. It ensures the reliability and performance of your vehicle’s electrical systems.

Keep your Ford F-150 (1997–2004) running smoothly with this detailed fuse box guide!

The cigar lighter (power outlet) fuses in the Ford F-150 vary by model year:

1997–1998:

Fuse №3 (Cigarette Lighter) in the Instrument Panel Fuse Box

Fuse №10 (Auxiliary Power Point) in the Engine Compartment Fuse Box

Since 1999:

Fuse №3 (Cigarette Lighter) in the Instrument Panel Fuse Box

Fuse №1 (Power Point) and Fuse №12 (Rear Auxiliary Power Point) in the Engine Compartment Fuse Box

#### Ford F-150 | 2004-2008
The eleventh-generation Ford F-150, a robust and versatile full-size pickup truck, was produced from 2004 to 2008. Renowned for its powerful performance, durability, and advanced features, this generation of the F-150 remains a dependable choice for both work and recreation.

In this article, you will find fuse box diagrams for Ford F-150 models produced between 2004 and 2008, covering years 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007, and 2008. These diagrams provide critical insights into the fuse layout and relay assignments, enabling owners and technicians to effectively troubleshoot and maintain the vehicle&#8217;s electrical systems.

What’s Included:

Fuse Box Diagrams: Clear and detailed visuals for quick identification of fuses and relays.

Fuse Panel Locations: Step-by-step instructions on where to locate the fuse panels inside your Ford F-150.

Fuse Assignments: Comprehensive descriptions of each fuse and relay’s purpose for diagnostics and repairs.

Whether you are replacing a blown fuse, addressing an electrical issue, or performing routine maintenance, this guide is an essential resource for Ford F-150 owners and technicians. It ensures your vehicle’s systems remain reliable and functional.

Keep your Ford F-150 (2004–2008) in excellent condition with this detailed fuse box guide!

The cigar lighter (power outlet) fuses in the Ford F-150 are:

Fuse No.37: Rear Power Point / Center Console Power Point

Fuse No.41 (2004–2007) or Fuse No.F110 (2008): Cigar Lighter

All are located in the Passenger Compartment Fuse Box.
